s.g: Contained by; inside.
s.x: The dog is in the kennel.

s.g: Within the bounds or limits of.
s.x: I like living in the city.

s.g: Surrounded by; among; amidst.
s.x: We are in the enemy camp.

s.g: Wearing (an item of clothing).
Expressing abstract containment.
s.x: There wasn't much of interest in her speech.

s.g: (obsolete, transitive) To enclose.
(obsolete, transitive) To take in; to harvest.
At or towards the interior of a defined space, such as a building or room.
s.x: Suddenly a strange man walked in.

s.g: Towards the speaker or other reference point.
s.x: They flew in from London last night.

s.g: So as to be enclosed or surrounded by something.
s.x: Bring the water to the boil and drop the vegetables in.

s.g: After the beginning of something.
s.x: The show still didn't become interesting 20 minutes in.

s.g: (in combination, after a verb) Denotes a gathering of people assembled for the stated activity, sometimes, though not always, suggesting a protest.
A position of power or influence, or a way to get it.
s.x: His parents got him an in with the company.

s.g: (chiefly in the plural) One who, or that which, is in; especially, one who is in office.
(sports) The state of a batter/batsman who is currently batting; see innings.
(not comparable) Located indoors, especially at home or at one's office or place of work.
s.x: Is Mr. Smith in?

s.g: (not comparable) Located inside something.
s.x: Little by little I pushed the snake into the basket, until finally all of it was in.

s.g: (sports, of the ball or other playing implement) Falling or remaining within the bounds of the playing area.
s.x: If the tennis ball bounces on the line then it's in.

s.g: Inserted or fitted into something.
s.x: I've discovered why the TV wasn't working – the plug wasn't in!

s.g: Having been collected or received.
s.x: The replies to the questionnaires are now all in.

s.g: Lying between; neither one thing nor the other; intermediary.
An interval or intervening time.
One who intervenes.
Synonym of inbetweener (“a person who or thing that falls between different groups or characteristics”).
Thorough; comprehensive.
s.x: in-depth analysis

s.g: occurring, or provided for use during a flight
(business, technology) in progress; underway
s.x: Several projects are currently in flight.

s.g: (gaming) Within the virtual world or player experience of a video game.
s.x: You can buy in-game currency with real life money.

s.g: (often in the plural) A relative by marriage (or through affinity).
s.x: The house got a complete going-over before the arrival of the in-laws.

s.g: Sometimes specifically a parent-in-law of one's child, for which the dedicated terms co-mother-in-law, co-father-in-law are rare.
Consisting of parts arranged in a single line.
(engineering, of an internal-combustion engine) Having all cylinders in a single straight line; straight.
(writing) Inserted in the flow of a text.
s.x: An in-line mathematical formula does not have to be on a line of its own.

s.g: (computing, of source code) Of a different language than the outer enclosing code.
s.x: BBC BASIC allows the programmer to write in-line assembly language.

s.g: (web design, Cascading Style Sheets) Of a style: inserted in the style attribute of an HTML element instead of in a separate stylesheet.
(chiefly UK, of training etc.) Taking place when one is an employee.
Relating to or being a full-time employee.
s.x: We offer both in-service and full-time employee training.

s.g: (transitive) To train or educate (someone) while they are working; to give on-the-job training to.
s.x: She spends most of her time in-servicing teachers in helping struggling students.

s.g: Existing or occurring within a single state.
s.x: in-state travel

s.g: Of or from the state where an institution is located, especially a public or state-funded college or university.
s.x: an in-state student

s.g: Applicable to or available to individuals of or from the state.
s.x: in-state tuition

s.g: (soccer) A ball that curves towards the goal.
(cricket) A delivery that curves towards the batsman.
